summaryText:
In this final message of the eight-week Changed series, Pastor Travis Hearn invited the church to live without lids. The service opened with a welcome from Erica and a testimony from Xavier Sorrow, who shared how he walked through a season of deep loss and grief, drifted from God and ministry, and was gently drawn back as God met him in his brokenness. His closing encouragement was that no one is too far from God's grace. The congregation then read a declaration of change together and heard 2 Corinthians 5:17, that anyone in Christ is a new creation.

Pastor Travis illustrated his theme with the story of fleas in a jar. After repeatedly hitting a lid, they stopped jumping high, even after the lid was removed. In the same way, many believers live under limits that God has already taken away. He named three lids to remove. First, the lid of lies. Using Numbers 13, he showed how ten of the spies saw themselves as grasshoppers, a description God never gave them, and he warned that what we believe about ourselves can shape the next generation. He pointed to Jeremiah 29:11 and Proverbs 29:18 to encourage seeing ourselves through God's eyes.

Second, the lid of labels. He urged listeners to stop answering to names like failure, rejected, or ashamed, and to answer instead to what Jesus calls them: forgiven, redeemed, loved, and free. He noted that Jesus called Simon, whose name suggests a reed, Peter, meaning rock, speaking to who he would become. He reminded the church that God calls things that are not as though they were (Romans 4:17), and that we are not our worst mistake.

Third, the lid of limitations. Using the picture of driving with the parking brake on, he taught from Judges 6 about Gideon, who was hiding and threshing wheat in a winepress when the angel called him a mighty warrior. Gideon argued with his own limitations rather than God's power, yet God answered, "Go in the strength you have. Am I not sending you?" The change came when Gideon believed what God said about him. Pastor Travis taught that the Holy Spirit already lives within believers, and that our greatest limitation is the one we have agreed with.

The message closed with an invitation to receive Christ (Romans 10:9, John 3:16), a prayer for those who raised their hands, and a prayer that lies, labels, and limitations would be removed, because when God is in it, there is no limit. The service ended with encouragement to share testimonies, to let the church know about decisions to follow Jesus, and to give.
mainPoints: Remove the lid of lies: the enemy does not need to hold the lid on if he can convince us it is still there, so we must replace lies about ourselves with what God says is true.
Remove the lid of labels: stop answering to the wrong names given by others, the enemy, or ourselves, and answer to the names Jesus gives, such as forgiven, redeemed, loved, and free.
Remove the lid of limitations: release the parking brake of fear, shame, and insecurity, and go in the strength God provides, because when God is in it, there is no limit.

versesMentioned.text: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.
The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
We saw the Nephilim there (the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim). We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them.
Now the serpent was more crafty than any of the wild animals the Lord God had made. He said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?"
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
You, dear children, are from God and have overcome them, because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.
Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.
As it is written: 'I have made you a father of many nations.' He is our father in the sight of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that were not.
The angel of the Lord came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to keep it from the Midianites.
When the angel of the Lord appeared to Gideon, he said, "The Lord is with you, mighty warrior."
"Pardon me, my lord," Gideon replied, "but how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my family."
The Lord turned to him and said, "Go in the strength you have and save Israel out of Midian's hand. Am I not sending you?"
If you declare with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.

Monday.scripture: Jeremiah 29:11 (NIV): "For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future."
Monday.focus: God's plans are bigger than the lies I have believed about myself.
Monday.action: Write down one lie you have believed about yourself. Next to it, write one truth from Scripture about what God says of you. Read the truth out loud three times today.
Monday.prayer: Lord, show me the lies I have been living under. Replace them with your truth and help me trust the plans you have for me. In Jesus' name, amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Romans 8:37 (NIV): "No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us."
Tuesday.focus: Moving from a grasshopper mentality to seeing myself as God sees me.
Tuesday.action: Notice one negative thing you say about yourself today. Each time you catch it, stop and say, "I am more than a conqueror in Christ."
Tuesday.prayer: Father, change the way I see myself. Help me surrender my thoughts to you and believe your voice above fear. In Jesus' name, amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Matthew 16:18 (NIV): "And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it."
Wednesday.focus: Jesus calls me by who I am becoming, not by my past.
Wednesday.action: List any labels you have carried, such as failure, rejected, or ashamed. Next to each, write a name Jesus gives you, such as forgiven, redeemed, loved, or free. Pray over the list.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, I lay down every label that you did not give me. Help me answer only to the names you have spoken over my life. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Proverbs 18:21 (NIV): "The tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it will eat its fruit."
Thursday.focus: Speaking life over myself and others.
Thursday.action: Send an encouraging message or speak a kind, truthful word to one person today. Remind them of who God says they are.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, guard my words. Let what I say bring life, encouragement, and hope to myself and to the people around me. In Jesus' name, amen.

Friday.scripture: Judges 6:14 (NIV): "The Lord turned to him and said, 'Go in the strength you have and save Israel out of Midian's hand. Am I not sending you?'"
Friday.focus: Releasing the parking brake of limitations and moving forward in God's strength.
Friday.action: Name one limitation you have agreed with, such as 'I am not qualified' or 'I am too old.' Take one small, practical step today toward what God has placed on your heart.
Friday.prayer: God, I stop looking at my weakness and look to you. Show me my next step and give me courage to take it. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 5:17 (NIV): "Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!"
Saturday.focus: Celebrating how God is changing me and sharing my story.
Saturday.action: Write a few sentences about one way God has changed you or met you recently. Share it with a friend, family member, or your church family, and thank God aloud for His work in you.
Saturday.prayer: Thank you, Jesus, for making me new. Keep changing me day by day, and use my story to encourage someone else. In Jesus' name, amen.

title: How to Break Free from the Lies Holding You Back | Living Without Lids
